tasks.short: Plan, evaluate or modify treatment programs

steps.what: Observe and interview patients about treatment needs and response
Analyze patient records alongside interview and observation findings
Plan or modify treatment programs within verified professional authority

tasks.design: Keep assessment, evaluation and treatment planning with the specialist using the {OTHER} clinical record. This design does not generate or execute treatment changes; decisions outside the specialist's authority go to the responsible clinician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Treatment evaluation depends on incomplete and changing clinical context.
tasks.enabler_now: Clinical records improve access to findings without removing the need to reconcile them.
tasks.still_hard: Interpreting response, recognising uncertainty and balancing the patient's goals.
tasks.human_edge: Relate direct assessment to the record and know when another professional must decide.
tasks.altitude: No change in treatment authority or clinical reasoning time.

reach.task: Prepare clear observations for treatment review
reach.learn: Treatment goals, response assessment and escalation limits

evidence.claim: Patient assessment and treatment evaluation require contextual professional judgement, not just record retrieval.

assumptions: Boundary covers specialist assessment and a treatment programme proposal, not prescribing or treatment execution. Actual local authority must be checked; the occupation label does not grant rights.

The specialist produces direct findings in s1 and reconciles them in s2. Treating professionals produce dated record entries through routine care outside this boundary, unchanged. Missing or conflicting findings require direct clarification within retained work.
No clean structured patient profile or free assessment capture is assumed. Programme wording and entry remain fully counted in s3.
Test native record views and care-plan functions before custom tools; no change is proposed.
Zero incremental upkeep because the task and tools remain unchanged. Overlapping treatment consultation time is allocated once.
unknowns: Local scope of practice and actual division of treatment planning
research_questions: Is there a separately measurable clerical care-plan step after clinical judgement is complete?

already_counted.description: Assessment, record analysis and programme proposal remain.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, net=0. Stable treatment review and uncertain response both retain assessment, analysis and planning; no autonomous judgement saving is claimed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Teach patient programs that support informed treatment decisions

steps.what: Select patient education content appropriate to the programme and learners
Teach patient education programs and check understanding of treatment choices

tasks.design: Reuse vetted education material from {DOCS} and retain the specialist's selection and teaching. Questions needing personal clinical advice are handled by the responsible clinician rather than answered automatically.
tasks.previous_blocker: Teaching must respond to different levels of understanding and personal concerns.
tasks.enabler_now: Vetted patient texts are available, but existing content does not remove facilitation or understanding checks.
tasks.still_hard: Keeping group education understandable while recognising questions requiring individual care.
tasks.human_edge: Explain uncertainty, notice misunderstanding and help people formulate their own questions.
tasks.altitude: Patient teaching and individual decision rights stay unchanged.

reach.task: Improve accessibility of a patient education session
reach.learn: Health literacy and accessible teaching formats

evidence.claim: Thuisarts offers guideline-based vetted patient education, as reported in the digest.
Live teaching and understanding checks remain human work in this design.

assumptions: Boundary includes content selection and teaching, not a separate programme-development project or clinical treatment consent.
The specialist establishes learner needs and selects the content version in s1, with all capture and preparation retained. No structured literacy score or free personalised curriculum is assumed.
Unclear needs are discussed directly; insufficient or outdated material is replaced through the existing clinical content route.
Review native education libraries first; no new app, generated patient advice or automatic translation is introduced.
Zero incremental upkeep because the current teaching process is retained. Individual information provision overlapping another task is counted once.
unknowns: Programme format and access to language or communication support
research_questions: Which parts of current sessions fail to support patient understanding despite vetted material?

already_counted.description: Content selection and live patient teaching remain.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, net=0. Routine sessions and sessions with difficult questions retain selection, teaching and follow-up assessment time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Determine required nursing orders from assessment within professional scope
Enter nursing orders using the selected actions and instructions
Check final nursing orders and authorise the exact version

tasks.design: Configure native order-entry structures in the {OTHER} clinical record for nursing actions the specialist has selected. Keep parameter entry, patient checks and full final authorisation with the specialist; the tool does not choose or execute care.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated wording can slow order entry, while patient-specific instructions require precise judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Native selectable order structures can reduce repeated composition without generating clinical choices.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing correct actions, conditions and review instructions for this patient.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise a misleading default and ensure the order matches the intended care.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated order wording; scope and authorisation rights stay unchanged.

reach.task: Improve clarity of a nursing order structure
reach.learn: Order semantics, patient identification and safe default design

evidence.claim: Native structured order entry can reduce repeated wording, while clinical selection and authorisation remain human.

assumptions: Boundary covers nursing orders only. Local professional authority must be verified; medication prescribing and treatment execution are outside and unchanged.

The specialist produces patient identity, action, frequency, conditions, limits and review requirements through clinical judgement in s1. Actual selection and field entry remain in retained s2 time; no structured order intent is supplied by a free upstream process.
Missing parameters, contradictory choices or an unsuitable structure return to manual order writing. No automatic substitution, inferred frequency or model-generated treatment is used.
Test native order structures and existing text reuse first. If already effective, the lower savings scenario applies.
Final review is fully counted in s3 and binds the exact saved order. Any change requires renewed authorisation.
unknowns: Permitted nursing order scope, existing native structures and repeated composition burden
research_questions: Do native structures reduce order-entry time after counting parameter capture and final semantic review?

already_counted.description: Clinical selection and final authorisation remain.
Parameter entry, exceptions and draft checking remain.

incremental.description: Specialist checks structure usability and changed protocol defaults.
Clinical record owner maintains authorised structures and tests updates.

approvals.approved_version: Exact patient-bound order text and all parameters, conditions and review instructions; any change requires renewed authorisation

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=82.5, gross=17.5 less two focal upkeep hours gives net=15.5. High assumes entry time halves through reusable structures; low assumes existing entry already works well and gains only offset upkeep. Assessment and final authorisation retain all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Assess patient discharge needs, preferences and unresolved care requirements
Confirm discharge support, responsibilities and follow-up arrangements with providers
Write discharge plan from confirmed needs and arrangements
Verify final discharge plan and communicate remaining conditions to patient and team

tasks.design: Use the native discharge-plan structure in the {OTHER} clinical record to reuse verified details and organise confirmed arrangements. Assessment, provider negotiation and final patient/team discussion remain human; the plan does not itself authorise medical discharge.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated plan entry consumes time, but availability and support cannot be inferred from old records.
tasks.enabler_now: Native structured care-plan fields can reuse verified entries without language generation.
tasks.still_hard: Confirming that support is real, sufficient and understood by everyone involved.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise an unsafe gap and resolve it rather than treating a completed document as readiness.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated plan entry; discharge and treatment authority remain unchanged.

reach.task: Help resolve an unmet support need before discharge
reach.learn: Care transitions, consent and confirmation of service availability

evidence.claim: Native structured discharge plans can reduce repeated entry, but assessment and provider confirmation remain substantive human work.

assumptions: Boundary covers planning through communication, not medical discharge authorisation, transport execution or providers' delivery of care. Overlap with discharge consultation is counted once.

The specialist produces patient identity, needs and preferences in s1, then named provider, agreed service, timing, responsible contact, confirmation date and outstanding conditions in s2. All interview, confirmation and capture time remains there; retained s3 time includes entering or correcting fields.

Existing patient identifiers and current care entries are produced during routine care outside this boundary, unchanged, and are checked before reuse. Missing or stale arrangements remain visibly unresolved and use manual planning; no availability is inferred.
Test native discharge structures and verified field reuse first. No custom integration or automatic clinical narrative is required.
Final review and explanation are fully counted in s4; changed arrangements void that version's release.
unknowns: Native discharge-plan functions, duplication burden and external-provider confirmation reliability
research_questions: How much repeated entry remains after counting all confirmation, capture and final review time?

already_counted.description: Assessment, provider confirmation and final review/discussion remain.
Plan entry, corrections and exception handling remain.

incremental.description: Specialist checks reused fields for staleness and reviews transition defects.
Clinical record owner maintains discharge structures and access controls.

approvals.approved_version: Exact patient-bound discharge plan with dated service confirmations and outstanding conditions; changes void release and require renewed review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=90, gross=10 less three focal upkeep hours gives net=7. High assumes repeated plan entry halves; low assumes gaps and manual corrections leave only upkeep-equivalent gains. Assessment, negotiation and explanation keep their full shares.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Clinical assessment and patient teaching retain their full time. Native order and discharge-plan structures can reduce repeated wording and entry after counting capture, checks and upkeep.
reach: Improve nursing order clarity with registered nurses
Coordinate discharge support with patient representatives
role.ambitious_version: A specialist with clearer nursing instructions and discharge arrangements who remains responsible for clinical judgement and direct patient communication.
